I'll revise the plan and write a point-by-point rebuttal that closes each gap.The plan is revised. I'll write the point-by-point rebuttal next.The revised plan is in `plan/plan.md` and the point-by-point response is in `plan/plan_rebuttal.md`. Nothing was implemented.

The major gap is closed with a mandatory golden-bytes test: a hand-built version-2 stream (top-level Put, nested Batch, empty Batch) must decode to those records and encode back to those exact bytes. Depth 8 is accepted from a hand-built 8-wrap stream, and every negative case decodes its unmodified base stream before the single defect is applied.

The other findings are addressed in the same plan: private and fuzz files stand alone with `priv`-prefixed names including `FuzzPrivDecode`; Put and Delete still reject oversize bodies before any append; the 9-byte bound is `minWireFrameBytes`, not `minFrameLen`; depth goes through one `childDepth` helper starting at 0; and the fuzz oracle requires byte-for-byte canonical re-encoding.
